case_name: Tata Tea Limited And Anr. Etc. v State Of West Bengal And Ors. Etc.
petitioner: Tata Tea Limited And Anr. Etc
facts: These writ petitions are filed by Public Limited Companies growing and manufacturing tea in the States of West Bengal and Kerala respectively.
The Petitioners in Civil Writ Petitions Nos. 5409-10 of 1980 are the Tata Tea Limited and a shareholder of the said Company.
The Petitioners in other writ petitions are Tea Companies and shareholders thereof and the Respondents are ranged on similar lines as above.

It is averred that the carrying out of the aforesaid processes is a specialized operation involving the application of modern methods of bio-chemical engineering.
issues: The challenge therein is to the Constitutional validity of Ss. 3 & 5 of the Bengal Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1980.

Whether the State Legislature has sought to assume the power, competence and jurisdiction to impose agricultural income-tax on the entire income derived from the sale of tea grown and manufactured by a seller.
petitioner_arguments: The income derived from the sale of tea grown and manufactured as aforesaid is derived partly from agriculture and partly from manufacture.

Under the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922 (referred to hereinafter as 'the Act of 1922') and the Rules framed thereunder the income derived from the sale of tea grown and manufactured by a seller has to be computed in the manner laid down in Rule 24 of the Income-tax Rules, 1922.
respondent_arguments: The State Legislature could only legislate in respect of taxes regarding that part of the income computed by the Income-tax Officer concerned as aforesaid which is treated as agricultural income, namely, 60 per cent of it.
By the said Amendment Act, sub-section (2A) was added after sub-s. (2) in S. 8 of the Income-tax Bengal Agricultural Act, 1944.
court_reasoning: The position remained the same even after the Act of 1961 and the Income-tax Rules, 1962 came into force.

As a result of this, a State Legislature could only legislate in respect of taxes regarding that part of the income computed by the Income-tax Officer concerned as aforesaid which is treated as agricultural income, namely, 60 per cent of it.
holding: The challenge to the validity of Ss. 3 and 5 of the Amendment Act whereby the said sub-ss. (2) and (2A) of S. 8 were omitted with retrospective effect and S. 25(4) was omitted is upheld.
